summary: The root شرذم (shirdhimah) refers to a small group or company of people. It can also mean a piece or portion of something. When applied to garments, it describes old, worn-out, and much-rent clothing.
lane: شِرْذِمَةٌ ذ A party, or company, ( طَائِفَةٌ ,) of men, or people: (S:) or a small company: (TA:) or a small number of men, or people: (K:) and so شِرْدِمَةٌ , with the unpointed د , on the authority of AA: (IB, TA:) the former occurring in the Kur xxvi. 54. (TA.) -b2- A piece, or portion, (S, K,) of a thing, (S,) of a quince &c.: pl. شَرَاذِمُ and شَرَاذِيمُ . (K.) -b3- [Hence,] ثَوْبٌ شَرَاذِمُ , (S,) or ثِيَابٌ شَرَاذِمُ , (K,) A garment, or garments, old and worn out, (S, K,) much rent. (K.)

[Hence,] ثَوْبٌ شَرَا ِمُ, (S,) or ثِيَابٌ شَرَا ِمُ, (K,) A garment, or garments, old and worn out, (S, K,) much rent. (K.)
